dl_h1:

dl_lead: In late 2025 Snapchat capped free Memories storage at 5GB. It first said anything over the limit would be deleted. It has since changed that: nothing is deleted, but from January 2027 Memories more than a year old that sit outside your oldest 5GB are archived. You will see them as thumbnails and need a paid plan to open them. Here is what that means, and how to keep everything yourself.
dl_tl1p: Memories used to be unlimited and free. Snapchat announced a 5GB free limit with paid plans for anything beyond it, and promised 12 months of temporary storage before anything changed.
dl_tl2d: Right nowYou are here
dl_tl2p: Snapchat says no Memories will be archived before January 2027, and that it will give notice in the app first. This is the quiet window to export everything properly, before a lot of people do it at once and Snapchat's export queue slows down.
dl_tl3p: In Snapchat's own words: Memories more than one year old that are not part of your oldest 5GB will be archived and remain stored on Snapchat. They appear as thumbnails, but you need to upgrade your storage to open, edit or share them. Your other choice is to download them.
dl_whp1: Snapchat keeps two things open for free: your oldest 5GB, and anything saved in the last year. Everything in between is what gets archived. For most people who have used Snapchat for a while, that is several years of trips, birthdays and everyday moments.
dl_whp2: And if you just hit Snapchat's own download button, you get a folder where every photo is stamped today, with no dates and no locations. That is the second problem SnapRescue solves.
dl_o2v: ✗ a monthly fee, for as long as you want to open your own photos
dl_cnote: Snapchat lists its 100GB Memories plan at $1.99 a month or $20 a year in the US, checked November 2026. Other plan prices vary by region. The plans keep your Memories in Snapchat's cloud and keep charging you. SnapRescue saves them to your own computer, once.
dl_ctah2: Get your Memories out while they all still open.

ba1_title: Is Snapchat Deleting Memories? The 5GB Rule and January 2027
ba1_desc: Snapchat now says it will not delete Memories over the free 5GB limit. From January 2027 it archives the older ones instead, and opening them takes a paid plan. Here is what changed, who is affected, and how to keep everything.
ba1_2: Is Snapchat deleting Memories? What is actually true
ba1_3: If you have ever saved a snap to Memories, this affects you. Snapchat capped free Memories storage, said it would delete what was over the limit, and then changed its mind. There is a lot of old information still going around. This is the plain-English version of where things stand and what to do.
ba1_5: For years, Snapchat Memories were effectively unlimited and free. In September 2025, Snapchat introduced a 5GB free storage cap. Anything beyond 5GB needs a paid plan. Snapchat promised affected users 12 months of temporary storage before anything changed.
ba1_6: At first, Snapchat's help page said recent snaps over the limit would be deleted. That sentence is gone. The page now answers the question directly: “Snapchat will not automatically delete your Memories because you do not upgrade.”
ba1_8: Instead of deleting, Snapchat will archive. Starting in January 2027, Memories that are more than one year old and are not part of your oldest 5GB are archived. They stay stored on Snapchat and show up as thumbnails, but you need a paid plan to open, edit or share them. What stays open for free:
ba1_10: Anything you saved in the last year.
ba1_11: Everything in between is what gets archived. If you have used Snapchat for years, that middle stretch is most of your library. Snapchat says no Memories will be archived before January 2027, and that it will give notice in the app before anything changes for you.
ba1_12: The short version: nothing is being deleted. But if you have more than 5GB of Memories and do nothing, from January 2027 you will be looking at thumbnails of your older photos and videos unless you pay. Exporting them is free and takes a few minutes of your attention.
ba1_15: Snapchat sells storage plans. In the US the 100GB Memories plan is $1.99 a month or $20 a year, and Snapchat+ and Snapchat+ Platinum include 250GB and 5TB. Prices vary by region. This keeps your Memories open, but they stay in Snapchat's cloud and you keep paying to look at your own photos.
ba1_16: 2. Do nothing and live with thumbnails
ba1_17: Your older Memories stay on Snapchat as thumbnails. You can still see that they exist, but you cannot open, edit or share them without upgrading.
ba1_19: You can request a full copy of your Memories from Snapchat and save it to your own computer. Snapchat lists downloading as one of your two choices for archived Memories. It is free, and it means you never pay a subscription to look at your own photos. The catch is that Snapchat's export is awkward, which is the next thing to understand.
ba1_26: Do this part now. Snapchat's export queue gets slow when everyone rushes at once. Requesting your data while it is quiet is the easiest way to avoid a scramble in January. What the 5GB cap actually means →
cta_h2: Don't leave years of your life locked in a ghost's cloud.
